metadata.journal: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology

abstract: PRISMA principles provide a thorough analysis of current advances in large language models (LLMs) and multimodal transformers for medical applications. As LLMs like GPT-4, BioGPT, Med-PaLM, and hybrid frameworks like COMCARE enter clinical processes, thorough synthesis is essential to increase performance, methodological adaptability, and implementation practicality in many healthcare situations. Their creativity in medical report writing, decision support, and diagnosis is notable, but the literature has not established a cohesive taxonomy that evaluates these models by uniform metrics, domain-specific generalizability, and ethical acceptability. Over 40 studies examined radiology report production, clinical question responding, cognitive assessment, and causal reasoning. After testing vision-language transformer architectures like PEGASUS and ETB MII for automated imaging-based reporting, graph-based reasoning was used to evaluate drug safety and interpretability of knowledge- integrated models like KELLM. As needed, BLEU, ROUGE, F1 score, CIDEr, and qualitative evaluations were used. Domain- adapted and hybrid models improve diagnostic accuracy, task- specific explainability, and clinician workload differently. Model illusion, biases, hostile manipulation, and resource-intensive fine- tuning persist. The report recommends strong benchmarking, public evaluation standards, and ethical frameworks for LLMs in high-stakes medical applications. This study defines LLMs' therapeutic utility and recommends infrastructure, ethics, and technology for safe and successful integration. This effort prepares scalable, interpretable, and equitable medical AI systems.

Abstract 
PRISMA principles provide a thorough analysis of current advances in 
large language models (LLMs) and multimodal transformers for 
medical applications. As LLMs like GPT-4, BioGPT, Med-PaLM, and 
hybrid frameworks like COMCARE enter clinical processes, thorough 
synthesis is essential to increase performance, methodological 
adaptability, and implementation practicality in many healthcare 
situations. Their creativity in medical report writing, decision support, 
and diagnosis is notable, but the literature has not established a 
cohesive taxonomy that evaluates these models by uniform metrics, 
domain-specific generalizability, and ethical acceptability. Over 40 
studies examined radiology report production, clinical question 
responding, cognitive assessment, and causal reasoning. After testing 
vision-language transformer architectures like PEGASUS and ETB MII 
for automated imaging-based reporting, graph-based reasoning was 
used to evaluate drug safety and interpretability of knowledge- 
integrated models like KELLM. As needed, BLEU, ROUGE, F1 score, 
CIDEr, and qualitative evaluations were used. Domain- adapted and 
hybrid

hostile manipulation, and resource-intensive fine- tuning persist. The 
report recommends strong benchmarking, public evaluation standards,

This study defines LLMs' therapeutic utility and recommends

Previous research showed LLMs can change 
medical diagnoses, report writing, and teaching. 
BERT-derived models, transformer architecture-
based models like GPT-3 and GPT-4, and 
specialist biomedical models like BioGPT and 
Med-PaLM were studied in recent LLM hybrid 
framework investigations. 
The most often used models were GPT-3 and 
similar models because they are versatile and 
adaptable 
to 
many 
clinical 
applications. 
PEGASUS and ETB MII optimized report 
production delivered correct contextual outputs 
for therapeutic application. LLMs provide better 
patient care, minimize physician workload, and 
improve education and diagnosis.

and

key_findings.claim: Med-PaLM 2 with ensemble refinement achieved 86.5% on MedQA, representing approximately 19% improvement over baseline, demonstrating superior performance compared to other LLMs in long-form medical question answering.
key_findings.context: Fine-tuned LLM for medical QA evaluated in PRISMA-based systematic review

key_findings.claim: COMCARE ensemble LLM framework achieved high F1 scores for clinical information extraction, with NER F1 of 93.76% and relation extraction F1 of 68.73% on biomedical datasets.
key_findings.context: Collaborative ensemble framework for context-aware medical named entity recognition and relation extraction

key_findings.claim: Llama-2-70B for radiology report structuring achieved MCC of 0.75 (English) and 0.66 (German), producing structured reports comparable to human accuracy with privacy-preserving local deployment.
key_findings.context: On-premise open-source LLM for automatic structuring of radiology reports

key_findings.claim: Llama 2 achieved sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 96% for liver cirrhosis detection from free text, with efficient local deployment requiring low hardware resources.
key_findings.context: Open-source LLM pipeline for clinical feature extraction focused on liver cirrhosis

key_findings.claim: Med MLLM for multimodal COVID-19 analysis achieved approximately 92% accuracy with high adaptability to rare disease scenarios requiring minimal labeled data.
key_findings.context: Multimodal LLM supporting multilingual and multimodal inputs for rare disease scenarios

key_findings.claim: OpenMedLM achieved state-of-the-art open-source benchmark performance with MedQA score of ~72.6% and MMLU score of ~81.7% without requiring fine-tuning, demonstrating that open-source models can eliminate equity gaps in health AI.
Integration of LLMs with CAD networks improved diagnosis by approximately 16.42% and F1-score by ~15%, enhancing patient-friendly interactive reporting.
key_findings.context: CAD-LLM integration for chest X-ray diagnostic accuracy and quality

key_findings.claim: PEGASUS fine-tuned for PET report generation achieved 89% clinical utility acceptance with a utility score of 4.08/5, enabling personalized physician-style impressions.
key_findings.context: Fine-tuned PEGASUS for personalized PET report impression generation

key_findings.claim: Larger LLMs exhibit bias magnification in generated text, with toxicity levels of approximately 15%, while producing more objective language than human-generated text overall.
key_findings.context: Linguistic comparison of human vs. LLM-generated news and medical text

key_findings.claim: KELLM knowledge-graph-enhanced LLM for drug recommendation achieved approximately 88% accuracy and 85% safety metric, addressing interpretability and safety constraints effectively.
key_findings.context: Knowledge-enhanced label-wise LLM for safe and interpretable drug recommendation

key_findings.claim: BioGPT outperforms other LLMs for BI-RADS breast imaging report classification with sensitivity of 60% and specificity of ~85%, though generalizability beyond BI-RADS categories is limited.
key_findings.context: NLP-based BI-RADS classification benchmark using ML, DL, and LLM baselines

key_findings.claim: LLMs are vulnerable to targeted weight manipulation attacks that can propagate misleading biomedical information, posing patient safety risks in clinical decision-making.
key_findings.context: Security evaluation of LLM susceptibility to factual tampering via targeted weight alterations

key_findings.claim: Multimodal transformers combining Vision Transformer with GPT-2 for radiology report generation achieved BLEU-4 of ~0.6 and ROUGE-L of ~0.65, outperforming recurrent models in coherence and accuracy.
key_findings.context: Encoder-decoder multimodal transformer for automated medical image report generation from X-rays

key_findings.claim: Domain-adapted and hybrid LLMs (e.g., MedFound) consistently outperform general-purpose LLMs in clinical diagnostic reasoning tasks across common and rare diseases, with accuracy ~85% and risk management ~90%.
key_findings.context: MedFound fine-tuned LLM evaluated across multiple clinical scenarios

key_findings.claim: CAD generative AI for pododactyl radiography reporting achieved BLEU-4 of 0.612 and ROUGE-L of 0.633 by integrating CNN and Transformer architectures, but lacks generalizability beyond pododactyl imaging.
key_findings.context: CAD system with generative AI for automated pododactyl pathology report generation

llm_extraction.methods_summary: PRISMA-based systematic review analyzing over 40 studies on LLMs and multimodal transformers in medical applications. Studies were classified by method, performance metrics, and clinical impact using an iterative comprehensive taxonomy. Performance metrics applied across reviewed studies include BLEU, ROUGE, F1 score, CIDEr, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), sensitivity/specificity, and qualitative physician evaluations. The review covered vision-language transformer architectures (PEGASUS, ETB MII), graph-based reasoning models (KELLM), ensemble frameworks (COMCARE, MedFound), and open-source models (Llama-2, OpenMedLM) across radiology report production, clinical question answering, cognitive decline detection, causal reasoning, and drug recommendation tasks.
llm_extraction.limitations: The review relies on approximation measures for studies that did not report explicit quantitative findings, reducing precision of some comparisons. Coverage is limited by PRISMA inclusion/exclusion criteria and may not capture all relevant LLM medical studies. The taxonomy does not establish a unified evaluation benchmark, making cross-study comparisons imprecise. Reviewed models exhibit persistent challenges including hallucinations, adversarial manipulation vulnerability, bias amplification in larger models, limited cross-domain generalizability, high computational costs, and dependency on high-quality annotated datasets. Several cited studies were limited to narrow imaging domains (BI-RADS, PET, pododactyl) with unclear generalizability. Real-world clinical deployment validation is largely absent across reviewed studies.

relationships.description: Review confirms Med-PaLM 2 superiority in medical QA benchmarks, reporting 86.5% MedQA score consistent with the original paper's claims of expert-level question answering.
Review validates Llama-2-70B's effectiveness for privacy-preserving structured radiology report generation with MCC 0.75 (English) and 0.66 (German).
Review corroborates findings on bias magnification in LLMs for healthcare applications, noting toxicity of ~15% and the need for improved fairness strategies.
Review confirms COMCARE's high performance in clinical NER (F1: 93.76%) and relation extraction (F1: 68.73%), validating ensemble LLM approaches for biomedical text mining.

methodology_details.approach: PRISMA-based systematic review with iterative comprehensive taxonomy classification of LLM and vision-language models in medical applications. Studies classified by methodology, performance metrics, domain application, strengths, and limitations using structured comparative analysis tables.
methodology_details.reproducibility_notes: Approximation measures used for studies that did not report explicit quantitative results; no original experiments conducted — all results derived from reviewed studies. PRISMA flow diagram used for study selection and reporting.
